The user is playing Monopoly as an AI.

I have $2111 and a pink monopoly with hotels. The opponent has $216 and owns most other properties, including brown and light blue monopolies. I am on ILLINOIS_AVENUE.

The opponent also owns a dark blue monopoly with hotels. All other properties are mortgaged, and the remaining players are bankrupt. I will continue my current strategy of holding onto cash and avoiding trades that complete monopolies.

I am 13 spaces from Park Place and 15 from Boardwalk. I will roll next turn.

I cannot land on the dark blue monopolies this turn. The next spaces I might reach are B&O, Atlantic, Ventnor, Water Works, Marvin Gardens, Go to Jail, Pacific, NC, CC, Penn Ave, and Short Line. Most are mortgaged by the opponent.

The opponent's next roll could land on my mortgaged Tennessee Avenue or on their own Illinois Avenue. I will not pay rent from any of these spaces.

The opponent is far from the pink monopolies and will pass GO before returning. I have enough cash to cover both dark blue hotel rents. I am now weighing whether to unmortgage any properties.

Unmortgaging Pennsylvania Railroad is not worthwhile. The $110 cost yields only $25 in rent, and I need that cash cushion for Boardwalk. Tennessee Avenue is also mortgaged, but the opponent already owns St. James and New York.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue is not worthwhile either. Without the orange monopoly, rent would be only $14 and the unmortgage cost $99.

I am now considering selling a hotel to recover some cash.

Selling a hotel returns only $50 and leaves four houses. The opponent has only $216, so they cannot afford to pay the reduced rent. I will keep the hotels.

I am now calculating how much cash I could recover by selling the opponent's light blue hotels. Each hotel sells for $25, and the four houses that replace it are worth $100, totaling $125 per property. All three light blue monopolies would liquidate to about $375.

I also calculated the liquidation value of the opponent's brown properties. Mediterranean and Baltic each have one house, worth $50 total if sold.

The two dark blue hotels are worth $1000 combined. I will not sell them because they are my win condition against the opponent.

If the opponent lands on a pink hotel, their cash plus the recovered houses would only reach about $641. That is still short of the $750 or $900 rent.

I am now considering trading for Park Place or Boardwalk to remove the opponent's dark blue hotels. I rejected offers that would give them cash or complete an orange monopoly.

I cannot trade properties that have hotels on them. The opponent would need to sell their dark blue hotels first, but they will not do that because those hotels are their only way to bankrupt me.

Liquidating all three pink hotels would yield only $750. Combined with the remaining $111, that totals $861. That is still far below the $2000 needed for a second Boardwalk hit or the $1500 needed for Park Place. One dark blue hotel hit would leave me bankrupt even after selling every pink property.

I cannot build or sell buildings to raise cash, and unmortgaging costs money. I need another way to accumulate funds before the next dark blue hit.

I will not pass GO this turn. The opponent has $216 and will collect $200 on their next pass, raising their cash to $416. That is still too low to pay pink hotel rent without selling buildings. I will end the turn and avoid any action that reduces my cash cushion or weakens my hotels.

I cannot trade for the orange monopoly because the opponent holds St. James and New York, both mortgaged. Acquiring railroads would not help against hotel monopolies either. The only viable path forward is still being determined.

I am now calculating the exact rent values for Park Place and Boardwalk. The four-house rent on Park Place is $1275, while Boardwalk remains at $1700. This confirms that surviving a single dark blue hotel hit requires roughly $2000 in cash.

The opponent's dark blue hotels would still be lethal even if they sold one to pay rent. I will keep my current strategy and end the turn. The next roll from Illinois Avenue lands on mortgaged properties or Jail and Community Chest, so no rent is collected.
